title: unify-terraform-private-state-layout-gpu-iam-networking-migration
author: Ethan Kim
body: Summary: This PR unifies the Terraform state layout for private deployments by splitting and restructuring state into three logical modules: gpu_node_pools, iam_roles, and networking. Motivation: current private private-state is a single monolithic state file that causes lock contention, slow parallel apply operations, and unsafe cross-resource diffs when customers scale GPU node pools or rotate IAM roles. The new layout reduces apply blast radius, enables independent lifecycle management for GPU node pools and IAM, and makes upgrades and rollbacks safer. What changed: 1) Introduced new terraform modules/private/gpu_node_pools that contains node pool configuration, autoscaling policies, taints/labels, and GKE/eks-specific provider wrappers. 2) Introduced terraform modules/private/iam_roles which centralizes service account roles, KMS bindings, and node pool IAM bindings with minimal cross-module outputs. 3) Introduced terraform modules/private/networking which isolates VPC, subnet, route, and firewall resources and exposes stable outputs consumed via data source shims. 4) State layout migration tooling: added scripts/migrations/replicate_state.sh and a terraform-state-migrate helper that copies resources between remote states with resource map templates. 5) Backwards-compatibility shims and data sources: small compatibility layers (private/compat) to allow existing configs to reference new modules without churn. 6) Example migration plan and runbook added to docs/terraform/private/STATE_MIGRATION.md and a canary plan for staged rollouts. Testing and validation: automated acceptance tests added under test/ci/private-state which run plan/apply/destroy flows against a synthetic AWS/GCP project and validate idempotency and drift detection. Load tests show reduced plan time when applying GPU node pool changes in parallel. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-1423) - [x] migration script implemented - [x] compatibility shims in place - [x] unit + integration tests added - [x] docs and runbook added - [x] staged rollout validated on internal infra Migration strategy: The migration is performed in three phases: Phase A (read-only discovery): run replicate_state.sh to inventory resources and produce resource map. Phase B (dry-run replication): use terraform-state-migrate with --dry-run to produce planned moves and surface conflicts. Phase C (cutover): perform final replication, perform apply in module-scoped states starting with networking, then iam_roles, then gpu_node_pools. Rollback guidance: rollbacks are supported by applying the previous module state snapshots in reverse order; the runbook includes exact terraform commands and safety checks. Related changes: updated remote state backend configurations to support per-module state locking and optimize DDB/tfstate backend for high-concurrency workloads. CI: introduced new pipeline job private-state-migration-e2e that runs in parallel with existing terraform-lint/format/validate jobs. Breaking changes: none for customers using the managed installer; customers self-hosting Terraform will need to follow the migration runbook. Release notes: see release_notes field for a short summary.
commits: feat(terraform): add gpu_node_pools module with autoscaling and taints
feat(terraform): add iam_roles module and KMS binding helpers
refactor(terraform): move VPC and subnets into networking module
chore(migrations): add terraform-state-migrate helper and replicate_state.sh
test(ci): add private-state e2e tests and canary plan
docs: add STATE_MIGRATION.md and runbook examples
review_threads: Ava Chen (2025-11-13): Left a detailed comment about node pool taint defaults. Request: make taints opt-out via variable so existing installs are not affected. Author reply: changed default to empty list and documented behavior in variables.tf.

Diego Morales (2025-11-14): Asked for tighter IAM role scoping and evidence that role churn won't cause node restarts. Author reply: moved node role bindings into iam_roles module and added note about role change impact; included test that validates node replacement is not triggered by role-only changes.

Maya Singh (2025-11-16): CI flake on GCP acceptance tests related to subnet reuse. Action: added deterministic name scheme and added retry logic to the test harness. Author reply: tests updated and re-run, all green.

Release engineering (2025-11-18): Asked for clear rollback steps and a dry-run mode for migration script. Author reply: added --dry-run and explicit snapshot checkpoints to the migration tooling and documented in STATE_MIGRATION.md.
merge_outcome: merged via squash (commit: a1b2c3d4) after approvals from Ava Chen and Diego Morales and green CI
release_notes: Unify private Terraform state into per-module states (networking, iam_roles, gpu_node_pools). Includes migration tooling and runbook. Improves parallelism, reduces plan/apply times for GPU node pool changes, and enables safer rollouts. Customers self-managing Terraform must follow STATE_MIGRATION.md to migrate state. No runtime breaking changes expected for managed deployments.
